quotes.text:
In the Sacramento region, @ucdavis' AI Institute for Food Systems is developing inexpensive wireless sensors to help farmers measure nitrate, potassium, and moisture levels in the field.  

Projects like this will make a difference for farmers & consumers for years to come. https://t.co/p6S8z65rmQ

I introduced the CHIPS Act to reclaim America’s global innovation leadership.

The investments in the CHIPS Act are enhancing domestic semiconductor manufacturing & bringing production back to America. These efforts will help us deploy AI & lead in the technology of the future. https://t.co/m73kdp5TaV

From closing the digital divide to AI to cybersecurity,      rapid American innovation continues to elevate the crucial role of @NTIAgov.

That’s why @boblatta and I introduced the first reauthorization of the NTIA in over three decades.
https://t.co/HLI6bJ9CZe

From deployment of next generation networks to managing AI—@EnergyCommerce Communications & Technology subcommittee is positioned to spearhead the policy that will shape the future. I’m honored to be reelected as Ranking Member by my Democratic colleagues.
https://t.co/4w3iI1MZJt https://t.co/o1bqeFZ72m

Thank you very much, Mr. Chairman. I want to thank all the witnesses for being here today. This is a critically important issue for the future of America and, really, for the future of humanity at large. [...] This administration's chaos and uncertainty will harm our AI leadership.
Mr. Turk, this dismantling of public research and reductions in the Federal workforce consistent with—is it consistent with strengthening U.S. leadership on AI and other emerging technologies?

As co-author of the CHIPS Act, I know how critical this policy is to strengthen our national security and technological leadership.

But @realDonaldTrump threatened to abandon this once-in-a-generation effort to bring advanced semiconductor manufacturing back to America AND his #tariffs are driving up costs for what we need to be competitive in AI, including aluminum, steel, semiconductors, and electronics.

Yet another example of this Administration’s harmful chaos and uncertainty.

Republicans are trying to hide a provision in this bill that would put a moratorium on states passing AI safeguards.

California not only has been an engine of AI innovation, but my state has also been a national leader in ensuring we balance innovation and competition with transparency and common-sense safeguards. To stall any state or local legislative progress on artificial intelligence, for a decade, is a slap in the face to American consumers.
To lead the world in AI, America needs fast, reliable, and futureproof networks to power AI-driven data centers, networks, and homes.

Our State and local governments are on the front lines of leveraging the benefits of AI while protecting consumers from AI-specific harms and ensuring workforce protections keep pace with rapid technological change. As home to 32 of the world's 50 leading AI companies, California is a national leader in ensuring that innovation and competition thrive alongside commonsense safeguards.

And that is why the 10-year AI State moratorium that my Republican colleagues jammed through in their reconciliation bill is so misguided and dangerous. We can't afford a 10-year hold on our States' ability to identify and protect the American people from AI-specific harms, not when AI is developing rapidly and spreading to all parts of our lives, and especially not without strong Federal AI safe guardrails in place.

To be the global AI leader, America also must lead on setting common sense guardrails for responsible and safe AI. Otherwise, we will harm innovation by damaging consumer trust and weakening protections for a fair, open, and competitive playing field where AI technologies flourish.

As the top Democrat on the @EnergyCommerce  Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, I led my California colleagues in demanding the removal of the 10-year ban on state and local regulation of AI in the Republican’s disastrous budget bill.

Without a federal AI regulatory framework, California has embraced common-sense safeguards that ensure innovation and competition can continue to thrive. As AI tools grow more sophisticated and more widely deployed, these state and local measures are crucial to promote safety and trust with consumers. That’s why 32 of the world’s 50 leading AI companies call California home.

The Republicans “Big Beautiful Bill” blatantly strips this ability to provide AI oversight, regulate AI implementation, ensure workforce protections, and protect consumers for the next decade. This makes no sense. It must be stopped.

AI is already a part of our everyday lives. Connectivity and artificial intelligence go hand in hand. The reality is, President Trump is undermining U.S. AI leadership by:

🚧⛔ Derailing our AI supply chain with tariffs

🎓❌ Gutting our AI talent pipeline by attacking universities and slashing research dollars

💸✂️ Weakening our AI infrastructure by freezing federal broadband funding

This is unacceptable. I will continue to fight for all Americans to access the resources and skills they need to capitalize on an increasingly digital—and AI-driven—world.

A 10-year ban on state AI regulations would’ve handcuffed states, endangered consumers, and put Big Tech profits over safety. That’s why I fought it from day one.

Last night, the Senate voted 99-1 to strike the moratorium from the Big Ugly Bill. Now, let’s finish the job—and stop the rest of this reckless legislation.

https://t.co/Tr2dFhG7Mi

When Republicans were trying to jam through Donald Trump’s big ugly bill they also tried to impose an AI moratorium that would have shut down state and local AI safeguards. I fought back against it, and it never made it into Trump’s disaster of a bill.
 
Despite overwhelming opposition, they want to bring it back. 
 
The American people know how irresponsible and corrupt this is, and so do I. I will use every available tool to make sure their second attempt at gross overreach fails again. AI can't be a free-for-all. It needs firm rules and real accountability to promote innovation and safety.

https://t.co/fe0bT1xgqT

I led 81 House lawmakers in opposing any attempt to reintroduce a moratorium on state and local AI laws in the NDAA or by executive order.

People deserve transparency, trust, and protection. We cannot handcuff states without any real federal safeguards.

We can lead the world in AI and protect our communities. That’s the future I’m fighting for.

https://t.co/4imiUp8Pgk

Trump Administration has thrown federal broadband funding into chaos—freezing funds, forcing states to redo plans, and ripping out affordability protections that help families keep service once the network is built.

Now they are threatening to illegally freeze $20B in BEAD funding unless states drop AI safeguards.

Their objective isn’t to improve life for the American people, it’s to enrich their donors. We must never let greed stand in the way of a more modern and connected United States.

As co-author of the original CHIPS Act, I have continuously led efforts to secure America’s technological future and to rip and replace vulnerable Chinese telecom equipment from our networks.

Recent attempts to smuggle $160 million in advanced AI chips shows a quickly evolving threat—and we need strong tools to stop theft at the source.

This week, I joined my colleagues to introduce the Stop Stealing Our Chips Act, to empower and protect whistleblowers and crack down on illegal exports.

America’s AI leadership is too important to lose. We are acting now to protect it.

https://t.co/jH2BAV5cDg

After Congress repeatedly rejected this idea on a bipartisan basis, Donald Trump has now chosen to try and force it through unilaterally. Trump’s order threatens states enacting responsible safeguards with costly, wasteful federal lawsuits and attempts to hold hostage the broadband funding Congress specifically authorized for our communities. This is illegal federal coercion, plain and simple. [...] With no federal AI framework in place, states like California have stepped up with common-sense safeguards that protect the public while keeping innovation and competition strong. These measures build trust and keep people safe.

This order would block states from responding to real, evolving risks. At the same time, it’s a gift to big tech—stripping away accountability when AI is becoming more powerful and deeply embedded in people’s lives. There’s a reason Congress dismissed this approach—it’s bad policy. I’ll keep pushing back against this overreach and defend states’ ability to put meaningful protections in place.

Donald Trump just signed an Executive Order to override state and local AI protections—the same moratorium I’ve been fighting from day one. With no federal AI framework in place, states like California have stepped up with common-sense safeguards that protect the public while keeping innovation and competition strong.

These measures build trust and keep people safe. Trump’s order would block states from responding to real, evolving risks. It’s a gift to big tech at the expense of everyday Americans.

There’s a reason this scheme couldn’t get through Congress—it’s bad policy with broad, bipartisan resistance. And I’ll keep pushing back against this overreach.

https://t.co/AIaQl0Sprw

First it was universities and social media companies. Then it was the press. Now AI companies. Trump has made it clear: no American institution or company is safe from government retaliation if it doesn’t fall in line. Anthropic said no to mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. Look what happened.

https://t.co/i2T4ZEzpDm

Through Trump’s AI Executive Order and now National AI Policy Framework, the administration has been bending over backwards to strip states of the ability to enact commonsense AI safeguards—all while there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
 
As Ranking Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, I won’t let the Administration weaponize broadband funding to bully states out of enforcing their AI laws. That’s why my colleagues and I are introducing the GUARDRAILS Act to stop this overreach and protect the public.

https://t.co/TMpHdzAT1c

Republicans keep trying to strip states of the ability to enact commonsense AI safeguards-at a time when there are no meaningful federal protections in place. President Trump's executive order is illegal coercion: it threatens states with costly lawsuits and tries to hold hostage the BEAD dollars Congress provided to connect every American to affordable broadband.

I have been very clear that the Trump administration can't use communications law as a backdoor to wipe out State AI protections. [...] That is why I coauthored guardians — the GUARDRAILS Act with Congressman Beyer, to repeal the Trump AI executive order.
We need that same balanced approach as we navigate AI. [...] Sweeping State preemption without strong guardrails is ignoring the lessons our most successful modern industry was built on.
The Trump administration seems to claim that because some State AI rules might affect telecommunications providers, the FCC can step in. Why is that wrong?

Congress needs to do the work of developing AI policy that supports innovation and protects people. But I have concerns that the Obernolte/Trahan draft goes too far in preempting states from responding to fast-moving AI harms. We should not take away states’ ability to protect consumers, workers, children, and communities, especially without clear, meaningful federal protections.

Any federal AI bill must be targeted and strong enough to meet the moment—not so sweeping that it blocks responsible state action before Congress has put real safeguards in place.

I co-authored the Guardrails Act to repeal Donald Trump's dangerous AI Executive Order, which sought to prevent states from setting their own AI policies.

Now, the NTIA is attempting to tie broadband funding for rural and underserved communities to a requirement that states abandon their right to enact commonsense AI safeguards.

When I questioned NTIA Assistant Secretary Roth about this blatant federal overreach, her response was as unclear as it was unconvincing. Americans deserve straightforward answers, not evasions, when states' rights and critical broadband investments are on the line.

But AI can also create new security risks. [...] We need strong guardrails for both open source and proprietary AI models, especially when they are used in our communications networks and other critical systems. [...] That means rigorous testing, strong cybersecurity standards, transparency, and clear accountability when systems fail or are misused. [...] And AI now allows criminals to clone a loved one’s voice, impersonate a government official, or create a convincing false emergency. [...] That is why I am working on legislation to prohibit fraudulent AI impersonations and improve coordination among enforcement agencies.

The people building today’s most advanced AI systems are issuing urgent warnings about the risks ahead. We must put meaningful safeguards including transparency, independent testing, and accountably in place.

That requires bolder action from Congress. https://t.co/9Gpmcc8kQS

Finally, the AI for Secure Networks Act examines how AI can help defend our communications from cyber threats. That’s important. But recent warnings from AI researchers and safety advocates make clear that we need to do MORE to address the risks from increasingly powerful AI systems. [...] We can’t treat safety as an afterthought. We need real guardrails, transparency, and accountability so AI serves consumers without exposing people to scams, cyberattacks, privacy violations, or other harms.

AI is changing quickly, and our responsibility to protect kids must keep up.

I introduced the bipartisan Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act with @Rep_Whitesides to establish safeguards for children interacting with AI designed to act and speak like real people.

When kids can’t tell where technology ends and a real relationship begins, the stakes are too high to wait. Congress must act now to keep them safe.

AI chatbots are becoming more common in children’s lives, and parents deserve to know those systems are not being designed to imitate a friend, express feelings, or build an emotional relationship with their child. The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act would require chatbots used by minors to act like tools, not human companions. It would help protect children and keep parents in control. Congress has a responsibility to put practical safeguards in place as this technology evolves, and protecting children from manipulative design is a common-sense place to start.

Congress must act on regulating AI — now. That’s why I’ve been working with my colleagues to introduce legislation that protects our national security, our jobs, and our children.

We can lead on AI innovation while putting the safeguards in place to keep Americans safe. https://t.co/4Jm4FEcf3H

I’ve never had a constituent ask for more robocalls. 

Yet the FCC is considering letting political robocallers reach your cellphone without your permission, including with AI voices. 

Making it easier to deceive voters weeks before an election is indefensible.
https://t.co/7ZBQiFXHuQ
Workers deserve a voice in how AI shapes the future of their jobs and a fair share of the benefits it brings.
